chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abu Al-Abbas Al-Fadl ibn Abdul-Malik, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not perform prostration (Sajdah) except upon the earth or what the earth produces, except for cotton and flax (linen).'
ai.seo_question: What surfaces are permissible for prostration in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* delineates the valid surfaces for Sajdah, emphasizing the earth and its natural produce while explicitly excluding cotton and flax, which are considered distinct from the earth's direct yield. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential preference for humility and connection to the natural world during worship, distinguishing between materials that grow directly from the soil versus those processed or woven. The exclusion of cotton and flax highlights a nuanced legal categorization where certain cultivated fibers are treated differently than raw earth or simple plant matter.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Abu Al Abbas Al Fazeyl Bin Abdul Malik who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Do no perform Sajdah except upon the earth or what grows from the earth, except for the cotton and the flax (linen)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from abu al-‘Abbas al-Fadl ibn “Abd al-Malik who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must not perform Sujud (prostration) on anything except earth or on what grows from earth except cotton and linen.’”
